To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the W decay to a heavy fermion via a light fermion can be treated exactly in the framework of the covariant single-particle inclusive approach.

(1) the heavy fermion production cross section for W boson decay to a light fermions via a heavy intermediate fermion with arbitrary mix of V, A, and T coupling is a function only of the heavy fermion mass, and (2) the electron spectrum from heavy-lepton decay is independent of the heavy-lepton mass.
(a) the cascade decay of W bosons is a very interesting topic that deserves more study, and (b) we have presented a new formalism for this problem, with exact analytic solutions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the decay $W^{\pm}\to \ell^{\mp}_1\bar{\nu}_{\ell}\ell^{\pm}_2\nu_{\bar{\ell}}$, where $\ell_1$ and $\ell_2$ are different light leptons.
the development of a covariant formalism to treat the decay of a massive particle to two or more fermions.
the decay of a heavy fermion to two lighter fermions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the cascade W decay through a heavy lepton is an excellent discovery mode, and that the cascade decay through a heavy tau is a good mode for measuring W mass, but not a good discovery mode.

, for the cascade decay W $\to$ heavy fermion $\to$ light fermion, the heavy fermion is not produced in a state with a definite polarization, and that, for the case where the heavy fermion has V-A coupling, the heavy fermions are produced in a state which is a linear combination of the V and A polarization states
, in general, there are no simple and reliable analytic approximations to the exact results.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the cascade decay of W bosons through a new heavy fermion is a very clean signature for the existence of a new heavy leptoquark.
it provides a convenient, compact, and exact analytic expression for the decay of the W boson to a heavy fermion and a light fermion in terms of the heavy-fermions' decay matrix elements.

we have presented the complete analytic expressions for the single-particle inclusive decays of the W and the Z bosons, and have illustrated their utility by a detailed study of the cascade decay $W \to H \to l$ where $l$ is the electron and $H$ is either a tau or a new heavy fermion.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a heavy fermion can be a useful tool in probing W decay.
the cascade decay of W to a light lepton via an intermediate heavy fermion is a very clean process with distinctive features, which can be used to identify new physics at the LHC.
the electron spectrum in W decay to a heavy lepton can provide information on the heavy lepton mass, the heavy lepton couplings, and the W mass.
